messages:
cheng: quick sync — nightly perf job flagged a regression when we run small-bert + vicuna co-resident on a single A100. observed much higher resident fragmentation and intermittent OOMs when kernel selector picks the fused attention for vicuna and a fallback aten path for small-bert.

maya: ugh. any flamegraphs / heap profiles?

cheng: attaching the clipped nsys output I grabbed from staging (snip). pattern is: repeated cudaMallocAsync peaks during model swap + sticky temporary buffers not being reclaimed fast enough.

cheng: ```
Time(ms)  API    Bytes  Count
1200      cuMemcpy  0     420
1210      cudaMallocAsync  524288  38
1215      cudaFreeAsync    524288  36
... spike correlates with kv cache repop and aten fallback kernels
```

ryan: do we have allocator logs for the slab allocator? are we leaking per-request workspaces?

sofia: i'm seeing in profiler that the KV cache refills cause >2x temporary buffer churn due to kernel switching. fused kernels expect a different workspace layout so we allocate new temporaries instead of reusing.

alex: two obvious angles: 1) make kernel selector prefer a compatible path if it reduces temp alloc delta; 2) introduce a temporary-buffer reuse layer keyed by (kernel_family, dtype, workspace_shape) with a small LRU.

maya: +1 on reuse layer. but we need to guard against pathological co-residency: two models fighting the same buffer pool and thrashing. Maybe soft quotas per model group.

cheng: thinking allocator tuning + routing policy: soft-partition VRAM into three bands — pinned KV cache region, per-model working set (soft), and a shared scratch pool. On OOM, evict from scratch first, then kv cache with an async prefetch fallback.

ryan: can we make kv cache eviction cheap? currently eviction triggers large memcpy to host and then back if reused, which is expensive. Maybe compressing small embeddings or quantized spill?

sofia: we already have a quantized spill prototype but it has perf cliff on restore. We could try a lightweight prefix-based eviction: evict older prefixes first (cheap) and keep hot prefixes pinned.

alex: for immediate mitigation: add a 5% guardband to workspace sizing for fused kernels; and change kernel selection heuristic to penalize kernel choices that increase allocated bytes by >10% for the current co-residency footprint.

cheng: MVP checklist I propose: 
- add temp-buffer reuse layer (LRU) + eviction metrics
- add workspace guardband config per kernel (default 5%)
- instrument allocator to emit per-model slab utilization and fragmentation ratio
- tweak kernel selector scoring to include alloc-delta penalty
- nightly perf job to run mixed-model co-residency matrix (small->large)

maya: sounds good. who owns the reuse layer? ryan for allocator infra, sofia for integration with kernel selector, alex for policy config. cheng will own the perf/regression harness.

ryan: i'll start a lightweight allocator PR that exposes metrics and a reuse pool. question: should reuse pool be global per-GPU or per-device per-sched-group?

sofia: per-sched-group (i.e., model family) seems safer to avoid immediate cross-model thrash. we can allow global fallback if pool pressure is low.

perf-bot: nightly/regressions: mixed-coresidency-suite failed (regression +12% median latency) — job id 2026-03-17-22:14 — linking traces in CI.

cheng: perfect, i'll pin those traces. alex please add an experimental routing policy that will force compatible kernel selection for canary runs (opt-in).

alex: will do. config sketch: ```json
{"routing": {"co_residency_mode": "compat-pref", "compat_penalty": 0.12}}
```

ryan: FYI cudaMallocAsync behavior: if we reuse allocations via cudaMemPool it's way cheaper. we should prototype wrapping our reuse pool with CUDA memory pools + async frees.

sofia: agreed. if we combine mempools + reuse LRU + kernel scoring we might eliminate the bulk of spikes. also add a prewarm step for evicted KV pages during model swap (prefetch in low-prio background).

maya: let's avoid big sync points during prefetch. background prefetch must be throttled and use low-priority streams.

cheng: ok action items: 
- ryan: allocator PR (mempool + reuse LRU) + metrics (ETA 3d)
- sofia: kernel selector change to include alloc-delta penalty + integration tests (ETA 4d)
- alex: routing policy and canary config + perf job matrix update (ETA 2d)
- maya: coordinate e2e canary runs and monitor traces (ETA ongoing)

cheng: I'll collect the traces and open a tracking issue with perf artifacts. keep thread updated with any quick wins. :rocket:

ryan: starting branch now, will ping when I have a perf graph.

sofia: adding test harness for 2-model co-residency cases to catch this earlier.

dev-bot: created issue RI-2026: "frag-aware allocator + kernel-routing to reduce co-residency OOMs" assigned: ryan, sofia, alex, cheng

cheng: thanks all. short sync tomorrow if anyone wants to pair on the mempool integration.

maya: thanks — excited to see the reuse pool in action :thumbsup:
